title: Local coordinate contributions and probabilistic additive models
pvg_object: many small prime-coordinate contributions to a global additive observable
ant_object: Kubilius model, normal order, and Erdos--Kac-type laws
forward_translation: Treating prime-coordinate contributions as approximately independent routes means and variances to probabilistic number theory.
reverse_translation: A limiting law constrains aggregate coordinate statistics but does not reconstruct individual valuation vectors.
preserved_information: first-order distributional behavior of separable additive observables
lost_information: rare arithmetic dependencies, exact local configurations, and exceptional sets
trigger: The observable is additive with variance tending to infinity or admits a Kubilius-type model.
typical_output: normal order, variance, or limiting distribution
error_or_wall: Approximate independence must be quantified; local models can fail for structured subsequences.
required_certificate: Verify the theorem's local size, variance, truncation, and exceptional-set hypotheses.
positive_example: omega(n) has mean and variance about log log n and a Gaussian limit after normalization.
counterexample: Restricting to a thin structured sequence can destroy the ambient limiting law.
anti_overclaim: A heuristic independent-prime model is not a proof.

title: Geometric exceptional sets and weighted impact
pvg_object: thin subset of valuation space carrying atypical height or support geometry
ant_object: density-zero exceptional set and contribution to weighted averages
forward_translation: A geometrically sparse set may have zero density yet contribute nonnegligibly to an unbounded observable.
reverse_translation: A large weighted error can signal concentration on a thin geometric stratum but does not identify it uniquely.
preserved_information: separation between frequency and weighted mass
lost_information: location and mechanism of the exceptional contribution unless separately analyzed
trigger: An argument discards a density-zero set while averaging an unbounded weight.
typical_output: tail bound or explicit warning that density alone is insufficient
error_or_wall: Zero density does not imply zero contribution for unbounded observables.
required_certificate: Bound the weighted tail, prove uniform integrability, or quantify the exceptional contribution directly.
positive_example: One point of weight N among N observations has density 1/N but contributes 1 to the average.
counterexample: Discarding the exceptional point as density zero gives the wrong weighted limit.
anti_overclaim: Almost-everywhere statements cannot be inserted into unbounded averages without tail control.
